summary: A seasonal forest waterfall with a small Gaumukh temple, ~15 km from Songadh just over the Dang–Tapi line — rugged approach, monsoon-only flow.
description:
Gaumukh keeps the old formula of hill shrines everywhere: a cow-mouth spout, a small temple, and a seasonal waterfall in deep forest — here on the wooded border country where the Dang jungle runs over the district line into Songadh taluka of Tapi. The approach is a rugged forest road and path of the kind that keeps casual traffic away; what arrives is mostly local pilgrim-picnic traffic, heaviest on monsoon Sundays and Shravan days.

The waterfall is honest about its season: reviewers photograph it dry outside the rains, and the temple-and-forest quiet is the fallback attraction then. In August the fall, the spout and the stream all run and the forest closes green overhead.

For this dataset's travellers it works as the northern extension of an interior-Dang day — the Ahwa–Subir–Songadh road passes close — or as a pairing with Medha waterfall on the Songadh side.
highlights: Waterfall-and-temple pairing in deep border forest
Rugged approach that keeps crowds thin
Pairs with Medha falls for a Songadh monsoon day
history_legend: The Gaumukh name — 'cow's mouth' — attaches to the spring-spout shrine tradition found across India; the small temple here serves the surrounding forest villages.

modes.road: From Songadh via the Don Gaumukh approach road — rugged forest driving for the last stretch
modes.rail: Songadh/Vyara side railheads on the Surat–Bhusawal line

access.last_mile: Forest path from the road end to the temple and fall
access.road_condition: Rugged and slow beyond the tar — high clearance helps, especially in rain

parking.notes: Informal clearing near the temple approach

visit.notes: Shravan Sundays bring the year's biggest local crowds; the fall is dry outside monsoon.

seasonality.notes: Strictly monsoon-fed — reviewers photograph it dry by late autumn.

experience.photography_notes: Temple, spout and fall compose together from the path; forest light is best before noon.

amenities.food: Seasonal stalls on busy days at most; carry your own from Songadh
amenities.guides: Not needed — the path is single and local visitors show the way

warnings: The rugged approach road punishes low cars — judge it before committing
Wet rock at the fall and spout is slippery; mind children near the stream

tips: Combine with Medha waterfall for the full Songadh forest day
Skip it outside July–September — the fall will be dry

nearby.note: Across the district line in Dang

images.caption: The spring-fed cascade over Gaumukh's fluted rock
